summary: ASTRONEX is a three-stage, ground-based physical training architecture designed to prepare junior astronauts for real Zero-Gravity, 1G constant-acceleration transit craft (RANGER-X concept), and rotating artificial-gravity habitats. Backed by NASA physiological and ISS data, it trains human balance, Coriolis adaptation, and 15-second emergency reflexes beyond computer screens.
details: Computer screens alone cannot prepare the human vestibular system or muscles for space physics. ASTRONEX bridges this gap with three progressive physical modules: (1) A Multi-Axis Gimbal and Neutral Buoyancy Lab to overcome Zero-G disorientation, (2) A Rotational Gravity & 1G Thrust Simulator inspired by established aerospace concepts from Konstantin Tsiolkovsky, Gerard K. O'Neill, and Brachistochrone transit trajectories—preparing crews for future rapid-transit vehicles like the 65m RANGER-X concept and phased rotating habitats starting with 500m tethered modules, and (3) A High-Stress Emergency Chamber using NASA Human Research Program (HRP) and ISS environmental datasets for realistic 15-second crisis drills.
